d0.intro: The Gyeongbokgung AR Rubbing Course is a hands-on walk following the 'fire-prevention devices' hidden throughout the palace. Rub the stone tablet that appears in your phone camera with your finger to take a rubbing, solve the riddle it reveals, and a 3D treasure appears on the spot.

points.d: Gyeongbokgung, built by King Taejo in 1395, burned down in the Imjin War, stood empty for some 270 years and was rebuilt in the 1860s. The wish that it would never burn again remains throughout the palace in symbols such as the haechi, the deume water vats and the bronze dragons.

At each spot, turn on the AR camera and tap the screen to raise a stone tablet. Lay hanji paper over it and rub with your finger to take a rubbing; solve the riddle revealed in the rubbing to pick up a 3D treasure. You can also try it outside Gyeongbokgung in demo mode.

Collect all five rubbings and the treasure chest opens. You receive a completion certificate you can print on A4 and 100,000P in treasure points, which can be exchanged for 1st–5th prize point rewards.
The haechi in front of Gwanghwamun, the deume on the terrace of Geunjeongjeon, the 48 stone pillars of Gyeonghoeru, the hexagonal chimneys of Amisan, and Hyangwonjeong with Chwihyanggyo Bridge.

visit.v: Gyeongbokgung 09:00–18:00 (varies by season · closed Tuesdays)
Gyeongbokgung ₩3,000 · free when wearing hanbok
5 min walk from Gyeongbokgung Station (Line 3) or Gwanghwamun Station (Line 5)
A charged phone (allow camera, location and motion sensors) · comfortable shoes

d1.intro: The Hanyang Fortress Course walks through the heart of Seoul, which Joseon chose as its capital. The wisdom of ancestors who chose the site by pungsu (reading the energy of the land) and hid symbols in palaces and gates to suppress the energy of fire flows through the whole course.

points.d: After King Taejo Yi Seong-gye moved the capital to Hanyang in 1394, the city wall was built along the four inner mountains — Bugak, Inwang, Namsan and Naksan — and the four great gates were raised. Pungsu devices to block the fire energy of Gwanaksan were placed in palaces, gates and waterways.

The bronze dragon of Gyeonghoeru at Gyeongbokgung, the vertical name board of Sungnyemun, Seonbawi and Chimabawi rocks on Inwangsan, and the royal tomb stones laid upside down under Gwangtonggyo on Cheonggyecheon.
The terrace of Geunjeongjeon at Gyeongbokgung, the city seen from halfway up Inwangsan, and the panorama of the old capital from the N Seoul Tower observatory on Namsan.

The dispute between Master Muhak and Jeong Do-jeon over building the city wall, the Chimabawi love of King Jungjong and Lady Shin, and the tomb stones of Queen Sindeok that King Taejong laid in Gwangtonggyo.

visit.v: Gyeongbokgung 09:00–18:00 (closed Tuesdays)
Gyeongbokgung ₩3,000 · free in hanbok · other sites free
Meet at Gyeongbokgung Station (Line 3) / Namsan cable car and circular bus
Comfortable shoes (Inwangsan section) · water · a jacket for the weather

d2.intro: The Hangang & Baekje Course shows that Seoul was Baekje's first capital two thousand years ago. The breath of the ancient age, when Baekje, Goguryeo and Silla fought over the Hangang, remains intact in earthen walls and stone tombs.

points.d: After Onjo founded Baekje by the Hangang in 18 BC, this area was its capital (Hanseong Baekje) for about five hundred years. In 475, Hanseong Baekje fell to an invasion by Goguryeo's King Jangsu, and King Gaero met his end near Achasan.
The huge earthen wall of Pungnaptoseong, Mongchontoseong and its moat in Olympic Park, the Goguryeo-style stone mound tombs of Seokchon-dong, and the view of the Hangang from the Achasan fortresses.
The walking path on top of the Pungnaptoseong wall, the 'Lonely Tree' hill of Mongchontoseong, and the sunrise observatory on Achasan.
Onjo's founding of Baekje, the roots of the Baekje royal family told by Goguryeo-style stone tombs, and the legend of General Ondal who died on Achasan.

visit.v: Outdoor sites always open · Hanseong Baekje Museum 09:00–18:00 (closed Mondays)
Sites, parks and museum all free
Cheonho Station, Line 5 (Pungnaptoseong) / Achasan or Gwangnaru Station
Light hiking wear (Achasan) · water · a jacket

d3.intro: Gyeongju was the capital of Silla for a thousand years. With royal tombs, Buddhist heritage and even an observatory that watched the sky, the whole city is called a 'museum without walls'.

points.d: Silla, founded by Bak Hyeokgeose in 57 BC, kept Gyeongju as its capital for about a thousand years. After unifying the Three Kingdoms, Buddhist culture flourished brilliantly, leaving masterpieces such as Bulguksa and Seokguram.
Seokgatap and Dabotap at Bulguksa, the main Buddha of Seokguram, Cheomseongdae, Cheonmachong in Daereungwon, and the Divine Bell of King Seongdeok (Emille Bell) at Gyeongju National Museum.
Cheomseongdae with fields of pink muhly, the stone-wall path of Daereungwon, Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond at night, and sunrise at Daewangam in Gampo.

Kim Alji and Seok Talhae, Queen Seondeok's three predictions, King Michu's bamboo-leaf soldiers, the Emille Bell, Asadal and Asanyeo of the Shadowless Pagoda, King Munmu and the Manpasikjeok flute, Cheoyong, Kim Yu-sin and Cheongwannyeo, the martyrdom of Ichadon, and Jigwi and Simhwayotap.

visit.v: Bulguksa 09:00–18:00 · Seokguram separate · Daereungwon and Cheomseongdae always open
Bulguksa and Seokguram paid · Daereungwon and Cheomseongdae area free
KTX Singyeongju Station → city bus / Bulguksa–Seokguram circular bus
Comfortable shoes · water · renting a bicycle in town is recommended

d4.intro: Buyeo was Baekje's last capital (Sabi), where the brilliance of Baekje culture and the tragic story of the kingdom's fall flow together.

points.d: After King Seong of Baekje moved the capital to Sabi (Buyeo) in 538, Baekje culture enjoyed its golden age for about 120 years, until the kingdom fell to the Silla–Tang allied forces in 660.
Busosanseong with Nakhwaam and Goransa, the five-story stone pagoda of the Jeongnimsa site, the Gilt-bronze Incense Burner at Buyeo National Museum, and Gungnamji Pond.
Nakhwaam seen from a Baengmagang cruise, the lotuses and pavilion of Gungnamji, and the Jeongnimsa site pagoda.
The three thousand court ladies and Nakhwaam, Joryongdae and the Baengmagang where a dragon was caught with a white horse, Gyebaek and Hwangsanbeol, and the spring water of Goransa.

visit.v: Busosanseong 09:00–18:00 · museum 09:00–18:00 (closed Mondays)
Busosanseong small fee · Gungnamji free
Buyeo Intercity Bus Terminal → city bus / combine with Gongju and Iksan in the Baekje region
Comfortable shoes · water · a jacket for the cruise

d5.intro: Jeju is an island whose people lived by relying on the gods amid harsh nature. Stories of the gods sung by shamans in their rites (bonpuri) remain here in unusual abundance.

points.d: Beginning as the independent kingdom of Tamna, Jeju has the myth of the creator goddess Seolmundae Halmang and the founding myth of Samseonghyeol. The oreum hills, caves and sea of this volcanic island became the stage of its myths.
Hallasan and the strange rocks of Yeongsil, Samseonghyeol, Seongsan Ilchulbong, Sanbangsan and Sanbanggulsa, and the coastal Olle trails.
Sunrise at Seongsan Ilchulbong, the Five Hundred Generals rocks of Yeongsil, Saryeoni Forest Path, and Hyeopjae Beach with Biyangdo.
Seolmundae Halmang, Jacheongbi (goddess of farming), the founding myth of Samseonghyeol, and Yeongdeung Halmang.

visit.v: Outdoor attractions always open · Hallasan trail hours vary by season
Some paid, e.g. Seongsan Ilchulbong · Olle trails free
Jeju Airport → rental car or bus (sights are far apart, a car is recommended)
Windbreaker · comfortable hiking shoes · water (weather changes a lot)

d6.intro: Seoraksan, with its strangely towering rocks and deep valleys, is a famous mountain rich in mystical legends of mountains and rocks and stories of temple foundings.

points.d: Long regarded as a mountain where immortals dwell, it has old temples such as Sinheungsa and Naksansa and countless rock legends.
Ulsanbawi, Heundeulbawi (Rocking Rock) and Gyejoam, Sinheungsa, the Gwongeumseong cable car, and Hongnyeonam of Naksansa (on the coast).
The Ulsanbawi ridge, the East Sea seen from Gwongeumseong, sunrise at Uisangdae of Naksansa, and autumn leaves in Cheonbuldong Valley.
Ulsanbawi that was late for Geumgangsan, the Rocking Rock, the miracle of Oseam, and the founding legend of Hongnyeonam at Naksansa.

visit.v: National park hours vary by season · temples always open
Seoraksan National Park free · cable car paid
Sokcho Intercity Bus Terminal → city bus / about 2.5 hours from Seoul
Hiking shoes · water · a jacket (it's cold on the mountain)

d7.intro: Honam, the old land of Baekje and Later Baekje and the home of pansori, holds deep stories of the rise and fall of dynasties and of women's heartache.

points.d: It is a land of plenty and stories: the legend of Gyeon Hwon who founded Later Baekje, Namwon, the setting of the pansori Chunhyangga, and Byeokgolje in Gimje, the oldest reservoir.
Gwanghallu Garden and Ojakgyo Bridge in Namwon, Byeokgolje in Gimje, Seonunsa in Gochang, and the Miracle Sea Road of Jindo.
Ojakgyo at Gwanghallu, red spider lilies and camellias at Seonunsa, and the moment the Jindo sea road opens.
The Tale of Chunhyang, the birth of Gyeon Hwon, Jeongeupsa (the waiting-wife rock), the maiden Danya of Byeokgolje, and Grandma Ppong of Jindo.

visit.v: Gwanghallu Garden 08:00–21:00 · temples always open
Gwanghallu Garden small fee · Byeokgolje and Seonunsa partly paid
KTX to Namwon or Jeongeup Station → city bus / plan together with Jeonju
Comfortable shoes · water · check the tide times for the Jindo sea road

d8.intro: The Folktale Yard is a course built around warm old stories for the whole family. It is planned as a hands-on course for enjoying the stories rather than visiting a specific place.

points.d: Long-told folktales like The Sun and the Moon or Heungbu and Nolbu carry the values of rewarding good and punishing evil, wisdom and filial piety.
Storytelling and shadow-play experiences, folktale-themed photo zones, and dokkaebi and tiger character missions.
The full-moon photo zone, the gourd-cracking corner, and the siblings' rope photo zone.
The Sun and the Moon, Heungbu and Nolbu, The Fairy and the Woodcutter, Kongjwi and Patjwi, and The Old Man with a Lump.

visit.v: Recommended for families with young children
1–2 hours depending on the program
Flexible depending on the plan, e.g. permanent or festival-style
Comfortable clothes (indoor and outdoor activities)

d9.intro: The Suwon & Hwaseong Course is a route where King Jeongjo's deep filial devotion to his father is engraved on the whole city. Along the route linking the planned city of Hwaseong, royal tombs and the temple of filial piety, you meet late-Joseon science and art and the touching story of one family.

points.d: In 1789, Jeongjo moved the tomb of his father Crown Prince Sado to Suwon, and in 1796 completed the planned city of Hwaseong. It was a city holding his dream of strengthening royal power and reform.
The Hwaseong fortress walls (Janganmun, Hwaseomun), Hwaseong Haenggung, Banghwasuryujeong and Yongyeon, Yungneung and Geolleung, and the bell of Yongjusa.
Banghwasuryujeong and Yongyeon, the fortress seen from Seojangdae, and the pine path of Yunggeolleung.
The tragedy of Crown Prince Sado, Jeong Yak-yong's crane, Lady Hyegyeong's 60th birthday banquet, and Jeongjo's filial devotion.

visit.v: Hwaseong Haenggung 09:00–18:00 · Yunggeolleung 09:00–18:00 (closed Mondays)
Hwaseong Haenggung and Yunggeolleung small fee · Yongjusa free
Suwon Station → Hwaseong circular bus / about 1 hour from Seoul
Comfortable shoes (fortress walk) · water · a jacket

d10.intro: The Pocheon & Yeoncheon Course follows the lonely back stories of fallen dynasties. Gungye who crossed the mountain weeping, Silla's last king who handed over his kingdom, and the shrine honoring them — traces of rise and fall rest quietly along the Imjingang.

points.d: In the turmoil of the Later Three Kingdoms, Gungye of Taebong fell and Goryeo rose; before that, Silla's King Gyeongsun handed his kingdom to Goryeo. Those final scenes are scattered across this land.
The silver-grass ridge of Myeongseongsan, the trail around Sanjeong Lake, the tomb of King Gyeongsun in Yeoncheon, and Sungeuijeon by the Imjingang.
The silver-grass fields of Myeongseongsan in autumn, the colors of Sanjeong Lake, and the Imjingang seen from Sungeuijeon.
Gungye's end and the Mountain of Tears, the only Silla royal tomb outside Gyeongju, and Sungeuijeon honoring the kings of Goryeo.

visit.v: Sanjeong Lake and Myeongseongsan always open · King Gyeongsun's tomb and Sungeuijeon 09:00–18:00
Small fees for Sanjeong Lake parking and Myeongseongsan · King Gyeongsun's tomb and Sungeuijeon free
Travel by car recommended / about 1.5 hours from Seoul
Hiking shoes (Myeongseongsan) · water · windproof jacket

d11.intro: The Yangpyeong & Yeoju Course travels back a thousand years along the Namhangang. A ginkgo that has lived a thousand years, traces of a great monk by the river, and the tomb of the sage king who created Hangeul — deep, calm stories flow on like the river.

points.d: The ginkgo of Yongmunsa holding a legend of late Silla, Silleuksa of late-Goryeo master Naong, and Yeongneung of Joseon's King Sejong line the Namhangang.
The thousand-year ginkgo of Yongmunsa, the brick pagoda and Gangwolheon of Silleuksa, and Yeongneung in Yeoju with the King Sejong History and Culture Center.
The Yongmunsa ginkgo in autumn, sunset over the Namhangang from Silleuksa, and the forest path to the Yeongneung shrine house.
Crown Prince Maui and the ginkgo, Master Naong and Silleuksa, and King Sejong who created Hangeul.

visit.v: Yongmunsa and Silleuksa always open · Yeongneung 09:00–18:00 (closed Mondays)
Yongmunsa and Silleuksa small fee · Yeongneung small fee
Yongmun Station (Gyeongui–Jungang Line) or Yeoju Station / about 1.5 hours from Seoul
Comfortable shoes · water · a jacket in autumn

d12.intro: The Haengjusanseong Half-Day Course meets the Imjin War victory and the courage of ordinary people on a hill overlooking the Hangang. With its short route, it makes a good half-day history outing with children and family.

points.d: The Battle of Haengju, in which General Gwon Yul crushed the Japanese at Haengjusanseong in 1593, is counted among the three great victories of the Imjin War along with Jinju and Hansando.
Chungjangsa shrine, the victory monument, the Hangang seen from Deogyangjeong, and the Haengju Victory Memorial Hall.
The Hangang view from Deogyangjeong, the earthen wall ridge path, and the victory monument.
The victory of Haengju and the 'Haengju apron' of the women who carried stones in their skirts.

visit.v: Haengjusanseong 09:00–18:00 · memorial hall closed Mondays
Haengjusanseong small fee
Subway Line 3 → bus / about 40 min from Seoul
Comfortable shoes · water · a light jacket

d13.intro: The Cheoinseong Half-Day Course walks through a site where people of low status saved the nation, together with stories of loyalty to Goryeo. It is a light half-day history course by car.

points.d: In 1232 Kim Yun-hu struck down the Mongol commander Salietai at Cheoinseong, and in late Goryeo the loyal subject Jeong Mong-ju was laid to rest in this land. It is a region where national defense and loyalty overlap.
The Cheoinseong site, the tomb of Poeun Jeong Mong-ju, and Simgokseowon.
On top of the Cheoinseong earthen wall, the pine grove of Jeong Mong-ju's tomb, and the lecture hall of Simgokseowon.
Kim Yun-hu and Salietai, Jeong Mong-ju's Dansimga and Seonjukgyo Bridge.

visit.v: Cheoinseong site always open · Simgokseowon 09:00–18:00 (closed Mondays)
All free
Travel by car recommended / about 1 hour from Seoul
Comfortable shoes · water

d14.intro: The Ganghwa Course gathers the origins of the Korean people and the history of national defense on one island. From Dangun's altar and Bronze Age dolmens to the Goryeo palace of the Mongol resistance and forts of the modern opening era, you walk thousands of years in a day.

points.d: Great scenes of Korean history overlap on this island: prehistoric dolmens, the Dangun myth, Goryeo's move of the capital to Ganghwa, and the French and American expeditions of 1866 and 1871.
The Bugeun-ri dolmen, Chamseongdan on Manisan, the Goryeo palace site, Jeondeungsa and Samnangseong, and Gwangseongbo and Chojijin forts.
Chamseongdan on Manisan, the naked figures of Jeondeungsa's main hall, and the walls of Gwangseongbo with the sea.
Dangun and Chamseongdan, Goryeo's resistance, and the legend of Jeondeungsa's naked figures.

visit.v: Jeondeungsa always open · Goryeo palace site and Gwangseongbo 09:00–18:00
Jeondeungsa and Gwangseongbo small fee · dolmen free
About 1 h 20 min by car from Seoul / buses from Sinchon or Yeongdeungpo
Comfortable shoes (Manisan hike) · water · a jacket

d15.intro: The Danyang & Chungju Course links the scenery and legends of the upper Namhangang. You meet the love of Ondal and Princess Pyeonggang, Dodamsambong where Jeong Do-jeon played, and traces of Silla and Goguryeo marking the center of the land.

points.d: A land the Three Kingdoms fought over along the Namhangang, it keeps the legend of Goguryeo's Ondal, the Chungju Goguryeo Stele and Silla's Central Pagoda.
Ondalsanseong and Ondal Cave, Dodamsambong and Seokmun, Sainam, the Central Pagoda of Chungju, and the Chungju Goguryeo Stele.
Sunrise at Dodamsambong, the Sainam cliff, and Central Pagoda Park.
Ondal and Princess Pyeonggang, Jeong Do-jeon's pen name Sambong, and the only Goguryeo stele in South Korea.

visit.v: Dodamsambong and Sainam always open · Ondal Tourist Park 09:00–18:00
Ondal Tourist Park and Dodamsambong small fee
Danyang Station (Jungang Line) / about 2 hours by car from Seoul
Comfortable shoes · water · a jacket

d16.intro: The Jinju & Tongyeong Course links the loyalty of the Imjin War with Yi Sun-sin's sea. From Jinjuseong, where Nongae embraced a Japanese general, to the Naval Command of the Three Provinces and the sea off Hansando, you follow the traces of those who defended the nation.

points.d: During the Imjin War, the victory of the first Siege of Jinju, the tragedy of the second, and Yi Sun-sin's victory at Hansando all unfolded in this area.
Jinjuseong with Chokseongnu and Uiam, Sebyeonggwan in Tongyeong, Jeseungdang on Hansando, and the Hallyeosudo view from Mireuksan.
The Namgang and Chokseongnu, the sea off Hansando, and the view from the top of Mireuksan.
Nongae and Uiam, Kim Si-min's victory at Jinju, and Yi Sun-sin and the Battle of Hansando.

visit.v: Jinjuseong 09:00–18:00 · Jeseungdang always open
Jinjuseong small fee · Tongyeong cable car paid
Jinju Station · Tongyeong Bus Terminal / ferry to Hansando from Tongyeong Port
Comfortable shoes · water · check ferry times

d17.intro: The Andong Course is a route where Confucian culture and head-family traditions are still alive. From Hahoe Village wrapped by the Nakdonggang and the Hahoe mask dance to Toegye's Dosanseowon, you walk the deep stories of Andong, the town of scholars.

points.d: The home of Joseon Neo-Confucianism, it produced great scholars such as Ryu Seong-ryong and Yi Hwang and brought head-family and seowon culture to flower, earning the name 'capital of Korean spiritual culture'.
Hahoe Village and Buyongdae, the Hahoe Byeolsingut mask play, Dosanseowon, Geungnakjeon of Bongjeongsa, and Woryeonggyo Bridge.
Hahoe Village seen from Buyongdae, Woryeonggyo at night, and a full view of Dosanseowon.
Ryu Seong-ryong and Hahoe Village, the Hahoe masks and young Heo, Toegye Yi Hwang, and the letter of Woni's mother.

visit.v: Hahoe Village 09:00–18:00 · Dosanseowon 09:00–18:00
Hahoe Village and Dosanseowon small fee · Bongjeongsa small fee
Andong Station (KTX-Eum) → bus to Hahoe Village / about 2 hours from Seoul
Comfortable shoes · water · check mask dance performance times

d18.intro: The Haenam & Gangjin Course runs from the end of the Korean peninsula to the reflections of exile. You walk the sunrise at Land's End, Mihwangsa on Dalmasan, Gosan Yun Seon-do's Noguudang, and the place of exile where Dasan Jeong Yak-yong designed Joseon's future.

points.d: The southernmost region of the country, it is a treasure house of southern culture where the literature of Gosan Yun Seon-do and the writings of Dasan Jeong Yak-yong's 18-year exile flourished.
The Land's End Tower and observatory, Mihwangsa on Dalmasan, Noguudang, Dasan Chodang, and Baengnyeonsa.
Sunrise and sunset at Land's End, the Dalmasan ridge behind Mihwangsa, and the camellia forest of Baengnyeonsa.
Galdu at Land's End, the cow founding legend of Mihwangsa, Gosan Yun Seon-do, and Dasan's exile and Mongmin Simseo.

visit.v: Mihwangsa and Baengnyeonsa always open · Dasan Chodang always open · Land's End observatory paid
Mihwangsa and Dasan Chodang small fee · Land's End monorail paid
Travel by car recommended in Haenam and Gangjin / about 4 hours from Seoul
Comfortable shoes · water · Dasan Chodang is reached on foot by a forest path

d19.intro: The Jeonju & Iksan Course links the city of kings with the dream of Baekje. You walk Jeonju, ancestral home of the Joseon dynasty, traces of Gyeon Hwon's Later Baekje, and the Baekje sites of Iksan touched by the love of Seodong and Princess Seonhwa.

points.d: Jeonju was the ancestral home of the Joseon royal family and the capital of Later Baekje, and Iksan was another center of Baekje, where King Mu placed a royal palace and Mireuksa.
Gyeonggijeon and the royal portrait, Jeonju Hanok Village and Omokdae, the Mireuksa site stone pagoda in Iksan, and the five-story stone pagoda of Wanggung-ri.
The Hanok Village seen from Omokdae, the stone walls of Gyeonggijeon, and the Mireuksa site pagoda.
Yi Seong-gye and Jeonju, Gyeon Hwon's Later Baekje, Seodongyo and Princess Seonhwa.

visit.v: Gyeonggijeon 09:00–19:00 · Mireuksa site always open
Gyeonggijeon small fee · Mireuksa site and Wanggung-ri free
Jeonju or Iksan Station (KTX) / about 1 h 40 min from Seoul
Comfortable shoes · water · walking in the Hanok Village

d20.intro: The Suncheon & Yeosu Course links Yi Sun-sin's defense of the nation with the ecology of the South Sea. From the headquarters of the Jeolla Left Naval Command to a Joseon walled town, a world-class mudflat wetland and a thousand-year-old temple, you meet a wide range of sights.

points.d: During the Imjin War, Yi Sun-sin built turtle ships at the Jeolla Left Naval Base in Yeosu and defended the South Sea; Suncheon is home to Naganeupseong and Songgwangsa.
Jinnamgwan in Yeosu, Yi Sun-sin Square and the turtle ship, Naganeupseong, Suncheon Bay Wetland, and Songgwangsa.
Sunset over the reed fields of Suncheon Bay, the walls of Naganeupseong, and Yeosu's night sea.
Yi Sun-sin and the turtle ship, Naganeupseong, Suncheon Bay and Songgwangsa.

visit.v: Suncheon Bay 08:00–sunset · Naganeupseong and Jinnamgwan 09:00–18:00
Suncheon Bay and Naganeupseong small fee · Jinnamgwan free
Yeosu Expo or Suncheon Station (KTX) / about 3 hours from Seoul
Comfortable shoes · water · a jacket

d21.intro: The Gimhae Course walks the myth of Gaya, which began with eggs that came down from heaven. The stories of King Suro and Heo Hwang-ok and the traces of Geumgwan Gaya, the kingdom of iron, are gathered within walking distance.

points.d: Gimhae was the center of Geumgwan Gaya, home to the myth of King Suro, the tale of Heo Hwang-ok's arrival and the splendid iron culture of the Daeseong-dong tombs.
Gujibong, King Suro's tomb, Queen Heo's tomb with the Pasa stone pagoda, Gimhae National Museum, and the Daeseong-dong tombs.
Sunghwamun gate of King Suro's tomb, the hill of the Daeseong-dong tombs, and the dolmen on Gujibong.
Gujiga and King Suro, Heo Hwang-ok who came across the sea, and Gaya's iron.

visit.v: King Suro's tomb and museum 09:00–18:00 (closed Mondays)
All free
Busan–Gimhae Light Rail, Suro King's Tomb or Museum Station / about 40 min from Busan
Comfortable shoes · water

d22.intro: The Hapcheon Course walks the mountain of the Tripitaka, carved with the wish to protect the nation. You meet the Tripitaka Koreana of Haeinsa on Gayasan, Hongnyudong Valley and the traces of Choe Chi-won.

points.d: The Tripitaka Koreana, carved by Goryeo during the Mongol invasions, is preserved in Haeinsa's Janggyeong Panjeon, and Choe Chi-won of late Silla lived in seclusion on Gayasan.
Haeinsa's Janggyeong Panjeon and the Tripitaka, Daejeokgwangjeon, the Hongnyudong Sori-gil trail, Nongsanjeong, and the Yeongamsa site.
The autumn-leaf Sori-gil of Gayasan, the lattice windows of Janggyeong Panjeon, and the twin-lion stone lantern of the Yeongamsa site.
The Tripitaka Koreana, the founding of Haeinsa, and Choe Chi-won who became an immortal.

visit.v: Haeinsa 08:30–18:00 · Janggyeong Panjeon open for viewing
Haeinsa small fee
Daegu Seobu or Seoul Nambu Terminal → Haeinsa / car recommended
Comfortable shoes (Sori-gil) · water · a jacket

d23.intro: The Miryang Course blends injustice, loyalty and the mysteries of nature. From Arang's Yeongnamnu to Great Master Samyeong's Pyochungsa and the midsummer ice valley, you walk the stories of Miryang.

points.d: The legend of Arang dwells in Yeongnamnu by the Miryanggang, and Pyochungsa honors Great Master Samyeong, leader of monk soldiers in the Imjin War. The nature legends of Eoreumgol and Maneosa are also famous.
Yeongnamnu and Arang Shrine, Pyochungsa, Miryang Eoreumgol, and the scree field of Maneosa.
The Miryanggang and Yeongnamnu at night, the Eoreumgol valley, and the stone river of Maneosa.
The legend of Arang, Great Master Samyeong, Eoreumgol and the bell stones of Maneosa.

visit.v: Yeongnamnu always open · Pyochungsa always open · Eoreumgol visits
Eoreumgol and Pyochungsa small fee · Yeongnamnu free
Miryang Station (KTX) / about 2.5 hours from Seoul
Comfortable shoes · water · a jacket for Eoreumgol even in summer

d24.intro: The Yeongju Course blends Uisang's Hwaeom Buddhism with the learning of Confucian scholars. You walk Buseoksa, touched by the love of the maiden Seonmyo, Sosuseowon, the first seowon, and Museom, the river-wrapped village.

points.d: Buseoksa, founded by Great Master Uisang, and Sosuseowon, Korea's first royally chartered seowon founded by Ju Se-bung, represent Confucian and Buddhist culture.
Muryangsujeon, the floating stone and Josadang of Buseoksa, Sosuseowon, Seonbichon (Scholars' Village), and the single-log bridge of Museom Village.
Muryangsujeon of Buseoksa with sunset over Sobaeksan, and the single-log bridge of Museom Village.
Uisang and the maiden Seonmyo, the floating stone Buseok, and the first seowon.

visit.v: Buseoksa always open · Sosuseowon 09:00–18:00
Buseoksa and Sosuseowon small fee
Yeongju Station (Jungang Line · KTX-Eum) / about 2 hours from Seoul
Comfortable shoes · water · a jacket

d25.intro: The Cheongju & Boeun Course is a route of records and Buddhism. From Cheongju, where Jikji, the world's first metal-type book, was printed, to Beopjusa and the Jeongipumsong pine on Songnisan, you meet proud cultural heritage.

points.d: Jikji, the world's first book printed with metal type, was printed at Heungdeoksa in Cheongju, and Songnisan in Boeun holds Beopjusa and the story of King Sejo's Jeongipumsong pine.
The Heungdeoksa site and Early Printing Museum, Sangdangsanseong, the iron flagpole of the Yongdusa site, Jeongipumsong, and Palsangjeon of Beopjusa.
The walls of Sangdangsanseong, Palsangjeon of Beopjusa, and Jeongipumsong.
Jikji and Heungdeoksa, Jeongipumsong and King Sejo, and Palsangjeon of Beopjusa.

visit.v: Early Printing Museum 09:00–18:00 · Beopjusa always open
Beopjusa small fee · museum and fortress free
Cheongju (Osong Station, KTX) / about 1.5 hours from Seoul
Comfortable shoes · water · a jacket

d26.intro: The Seosan & Yesan Course is a Naepo route linking the Smile of Baekje with traces of Joseon scholars. You walk from a Baekje Buddha carved in rock to Haemieupseong and the old house of Chusa Kim Jeong-hui.

points.d: The Rock-carved Buddha Triad called the Smile of Baekje and the Bowonsa site convey Baekje Buddhism, while Haemieupseong and Chusa's old house tell of Joseon's history and art.
The Rock-carved Buddha Triad of Seosan, the Bowonsa site, Haemieupseong, the main hall of Sudeoksa, and Chusa's old house.
The smile of the Buddha Triad, the walls of Haemieupseong, and the main hall of Sudeoksa.
The Smile of Baekje, Haemieupseong, and Chusa Kim Jeong-hui with Sehando.

visit.v: Buddha Triad and Haemieupseong 09:00–18:00 · Sudeoksa always open
Haemieupseong and Sudeoksa small fee · Buddha Triad free
Travel by car recommended in Seosan and Yesan / about 2 hours from Seoul
Comfortable shoes · water

d27.intro: The Gangneung Course walks the hometown of Saimdang and Yulgok, a city of sea and festivals. From Ojukheon to Gyeongpodae, the East Sea and the traces of the thousand-year Danoje festival.

points.d: Shin Saimdang and Yulgok Yi I were born and raised at Ojukheon, and the Gangneung Danoje is a world-renowned festival that has continued for over a thousand years.
Ojukheon, Gyeongpodae and Gyeongpo Lake, Seongyojang, the Guksa Seonghwang shrine on Daegwallyeong, and Jeongdongjin.
Gyeongpo Lake and the East Sea, Mongnyongsil at Ojukheon, and sunrise at Jeongdongjin.
Shin Saimdang and Yulgok, the five moons of Gyeongpodae, and the Gangneung Danoje.

visit.v: Ojukheon and Seongyojang 09:00–18:00 · Gyeongpodae always open
Ojukheon and Seongyojang small fee · Gyeongpodae free
Gangneung Station (KTX) / about 2 hours from Seoul
Comfortable shoes · water · a jacket for the sea breeze

d28.intro: The Yeongwol Course follows the sad history of the boy king Danjong. From his place of exile at Cheongnyeongpo to his tomb Jangneung and the river-bend scenery of the Seogang, you walk Yeongwol's story.

points.d: Danjong lost his throne to Sejo, was exiled to Yeongwol and ended his short life here; the local official Eom Heung-do recovered his body, and the spot became Jangneung.
Cheongnyeongpo and Gwaneumsong, Gwanpungheon and Jagyuru, Jangneung, Seondol, and the Korean Peninsula-shaped terrain.
The pine grove of Cheongnyeongpo, the Seondol observatory, and the Korean Peninsula terrain observatory.
Danjong's exile and Cheongnyeongpo, the loyal Eom Heung-do, and the sad tale of Danjong.

visit.v: Cheongnyeongpo and Jangneung 09:00–18:00 (ferry operates)
Cheongnyeongpo and Jangneung small fee
Travel by car recommended in Yeongwol / about 2.5 hours from Seoul
Comfortable shoes · water · check the Cheongnyeongpo ferry times

d29.intro: The Busan Course links the history of national defense with stunning sea views. From Dongnaeseong, first battlefield of the Imjin War, to Beomeosa on Geumjeongsan, Haeundae and Taejongdae, you walk Busan, city of mountains and sea, in one day.

points.d: Dongnaeseong, defended by Song Sang-hyeon in the Imjin War, and the Gaya–Silla Bokcheon-dong tombs tell of old Busan, while Beomeosa, Haeundae and Taejongdae carry the legends of a sea city.
Dongnae Eupseong and its north gate, the Bokcheon-dong tombs, Beomeosa on Geumjeongsan, Dongbaekseom in Haeundae, and Sinseondae at Taejongdae.
The cliffs and lighthouse of Taejongdae, Dongbaekseom in Haeundae, and the Iljumun gate of Beomeosa.
Song Sang-hyeon and Dongnaeseong, Geumsaem and Beomeosa, and Choe Chi-won and Haeundae.

visit.v: Beomeosa always open · Taejongdae Danubi train runs · Bokcheon Museum closed Mondays
Mostly free · Taejongdae train paid
Busan subway and city buses / about 2 h 40 min from Seoul by KTX
Comfortable shoes · water · a jacket for the sea breeze

d30.intro: The Daegu Course walks the Buddhist culture and defense history of Palgongsan. From Donghwasa and Gatbawi, said to grant wishes, to the traces of Sin Sung-gyeom, the loyal general who saved Wang Geon, you explore the embrace of Palgongsan.

points.d: Palgongsan was the stage of Silla Buddhism and the founding of Goryeo, home to Donghwasa, Buinsa, Gatbawi and the sites of Sin Sung-gyeom from the Battle of Gongsan.
The Unification Medicine Buddha of Donghwasa, Gatbawi on Gwanbong, Pagyesa, Buinsa, and the General Sin Sung-gyeom historic site.
The view from the top of Gatbawi, the great Buddha of Donghwasa, and Palgongsan's autumn leaves.
Donghwasa, wishing at Gatbawi, and the Battle of Gongsan with Sin Sung-gyeom.

visit.v: Donghwasa and Gatbawi always open · cable car operates
Donghwasa small fee · Gatbawi free · cable car paid
Daegu subway + bus / about 1 h 50 min from Seoul by KTX
Hiking shoes (Gatbawi stairs) · water · a jacket

d31.intro: The Daejeon Course walks a city where the spirit of filial piety and scholarship flows. From Dongchundang and Uam Historic Park of Hoedeok's scholar culture to the red-clay trail of Gyejoksan and Ppuri Park.

points.d: Hoedeok was the center of late-Joseon scholar culture that produced great scholars like Song Si-yeol and Song Jun-gil, and Gyejoksanseong preserves traces of Baekje.
Dongchundang, Uam Historic Park and Namganjeongsa, the red-clay trail of Gyejoksanseong, Bomunsan, and Ppuri Park.
The Gyejoksan red-clay trail, the pond of Namganjeongsa, and the Bomunsan observatory.
Uam Song Si-yeol, Dongchundang Song Jun-gil, and Ppuri Park of filial piety.

visit.v: Dongchundang and Uam Historic Park always open · Ppuri Park 09:00–18:00
Mostly free
Daejeon Station (KTX) and city buses / about 1 hour from Seoul
Comfortable shoes · water · a towel for the barefoot trail on Gyejoksan

d32.intro: The Ulsan Course links prehistoric rock art with the sea of Cheoyong. From the Bangudae Petroglyphs and Cheonjeon-ri rock to Daewangam, Cheoyongam and the sea at Ganjeolgot, you walk back through time.

points.d: The prehistoric rock art of Bangudae and Cheonjeon-ri, along with Silla's Cheoyong tale and the legend of King Munmu's queen, are found together along Ulsan's sea and rivers.
The Bangudae Petroglyphs, the Cheonjeon-ri Petroglyphs, Daewangam Park, Cheoyongam, and Ganjeolgot.
The sea and suspension bridge at Daewangam, the Bangudae cliff, and sunrise at Ganjeolgot.
The whale drawings of Bangudae, Cheoyong and Cheoyongam, and Daewangam with King Munmu's queen.

visit.v: Bangudae and Daewangam always open · Petroglyph Museum closed Mondays
Mostly free
Ulsan Station (KTX) and city buses / car recommended
Comfortable shoes · water · a jacket for the sea breeze · binoculars

d33.intro: The Gwangju Course embraces Mudeungsan in a city where righteousness and art flow. From the columnar joints of Ipseokdae and Jeungsimsa to shrines honoring righteous army leaders and the modern history village of Yangnim-dong.

points.d: Mudeungsan's natural heritage, the loyalty of Imjin War righteous army leaders Kim Deok-ryeong and Go Gyeong-myeong, and early-20th-century Yangnim-dong make up Gwangju, the 'town of righteousness and art'.
Ipseokdae and Seoseokdae on Mudeungsan, Jeungsimsa, Chungjangsa, Pochungsa, and Yangnim-dong History Village.
The columnar joints of Mudeungsan, and Penguin Village and the modern alleys of Yangnim-dong.
Ipseokdae of Mudeungsan, the righteous army leader Kim Deok-ryeong, and Go Gyeong-myeong's martyrdom.

visit.v: Mudeungsan trails and Jeungsimsa always open · Chungjangsa and Pochungsa 09:00–18:00
Mostly free
Gwangju Songjeong Station (KTX) and city buses / Mudeungsan shuttle
Hiking shoes (Ipseokdae) · water · a jacket

d34.intro: The Sejong Course links Baekje's last dream with the city of Hangeul. From Unjusanseong of the Baekje restoration movement and Biamsa, temple of the refugees, to Ieung Bridge over the Geumgang and the observatory.

points.d: Unjusanseong, where the restoration movement unfolded after Baekje fell, and Biamsa, the refugees' temple, tell of Baekje's end, while the administrative city named after King Sejong tells of today.
Unjusanseong, Biamsa and its Buddhist stele, Yeongi Hyanggyo, Ieung Bridge over the Geumgang, and Milmaru Observatory.
Ieung Bridge at night, the Geumgang with Sejong's new downtown, and the view from Unjusanseong.
The Baekje restoration movement, the refugees of Biamsa, and Ieung Bridge modeled on Hangeul.

visit.v: Biamsa and Hyanggyo always open · Ieung Bridge night lighting
All free
Osong Station (KTX) → BRT / about 1.5 hours from Seoul
Comfortable shoes · water · a jacket
